stories.headline: OpenAI claims formal proof for Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
stories.confirmed_fact: OpenAI has published a 160-page formal proof using an internal AI system that claims to demonstrate a finite-time blowup in the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
stories.why_it_matters: If verified, this would represent a historic breakthrough in fluid dynamics and a significant validation of AI's capability to solve complex, long-standing mathematical problems.
stories.interpretation: The reliance on an unverified, proprietary system and the subsequent controversy regarding potential data usage highlights the growing tension between rapid AI-driven scientific discovery and the traditional peer-review process.
stories.source_title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem

stories.headline: Anthropic excludes UK AISI from pre-release testing of Claude Mythos 5.1
stories.confirmed_fact: Anthropic has restricted pre-release safety testing for its new Claude Mythos 5.1 model to US-based organizations, declining access to the UK's AI Security Institute.
stories.why_it_matters: This move marks a potential shift toward regional protectionism in AI safety, raising concerns among UK officials about the influence of US-centric regulatory frameworks on global AI development.
stories.interpretation: The decision suggests that AI labs may be prioritizing alignment with US administration export controls and security protocols over international collaborative safety testing.
stories.source_title: Sources: Anthropic declined to submit Mythos 5.1 to the UK AISI for pre-release testing, prompting UK fears that US AI labs are aligning with US protectionism (Financial Times)

stories.headline: Google commits €13B to Finnish AI infrastructure
stories.confirmed_fact: Google announced a €13 billion investment in Finland for 2027–2028, including the construction of three new data centers and a 22-year nuclear power purchase agreement.
stories.why_it_matters: This represents Google's largest European infrastructure investment, highlighting the massive energy and physical footprint required to sustain large-scale AI operations.
stories.interpretation: The long-term nuclear power agreement indicates that tech giants are increasingly seeking to secure stable, carbon-free energy sources to mitigate the power-grid pressures associated with AI scaling.
stories.source_title: Google plans to invest €13B+ in Finland over two years, its biggest investment in Europe to date, to build three new data centers and expand an existing one (Kirsi Heikel/Bloomberg)

stories.headline: Anthropic alignment lead cites >10% existential risk from AI
stories.confirmed_fact: Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science lead at Anthropic, stated he personally estimates a greater than 10% chance of AI-caused human extinction within the next decade.
stories.why_it_matters: Public statements from senior safety researchers regarding the lack of a clear alignment plan for superintelligence underscore the internal uncertainty surrounding the long-term safety of advanced AI models.
stories.interpretation: The disclosure, occurring alongside staff resignations, reflects a growing divide between the rapid deployment of AI capabilities and the current state of alignment research.
stories.source_title: Anthropic's Alignment Science lead says there is a ">10%" chance AI could kill all humans within the next decade and worries about recursive self-improvement (Evan Hubinger/@evanhub)

practical_takeaway: Organizations should monitor the increasing regionalization of AI safety standards and the rising costs of data center infrastructure, as these factors may influence future access to models and the stability of AI-driven workflows.
watch_next: Observe how the international mathematics community responds to the OpenAI Navier–Stokes proof and whether further AI labs follow Anthropic's lead in restricting model access to specific national safety institutes.
